item.title: Mapping the Landscape of Informal Transit Systems in Africa: A Systematic Review of Evidence and Emerging Themes
item.description:
Robert Nutifafa Arku, Elmond Bandauko, Kofi Bonsu, Eunice Naa Odarley Lamptey, Mwendwa Kiko, Leonard Mwesigwa, Dennis Owusu Nimoh
Journal of Planning Literature
DOI: 10.1177/08854122261503328
This review paper examines how the literature conceptualizes informal transit systems in urban processes across Africa. Drawing on a systematic review, we identify nine dominant themes, spanning mapping informal transit systems to COVID-19 impacts. We characterize the literature as broad in scope and increasingly engaged with the complexity of informal transit systems through innovative methods tailored to dynamic and data-scarce contexts. However, the field remains analytically uneven, with greater depth still needed. Consequently, we identify four priority directions for advancing research: longitudinal analysis, deeper engagement with institutional processes, more focus on distributional equity, and assessment of potential impacts of technology-based external disruptors such as autonomous vehicles and artificial intelligence.
